item.title: After a bicycle crash, some motorcyclists stopped to help
item.description: A photojournalist was stuck, injured and without cell service, after he crashed into a boulder on his bicycle in Scotland. Three motorcyclists stopped to help.
item.content:encoded: A photojournalist was stuck, injured and without cell service, after he crashed into a boulder on his bicycle in Scotland. Three motorcyclists stopped to help.

item.title: How television and literature wrestled with 9/11
item.description: Over the past 25 years, books and television series have reflected the events and fallout from 9/11 in both direct and indirect ways.

item.title: Conductor Julian Wachner receives suspended sentence for possession of child sex abuse material
item.description: The formerly prominent, widely recorded conductor was sentenced Wednesday to nearly six years of probation for five counts of possession of child sex abuse material in Indianapolis.

item.title: How the Sept. 11 attacks remade life in America
item.description: In Homeland: The War on Terror in American Life, Richard Beck links the attacks to an expansion of government surveillance, increased hate crimes against Muslim Americans and the rise of Donald Trump.

item.title: It's 2031, and the U.S. has 'come undone' in Emily St. John Mandel's 'Exit Party'
item.description: Exit Party presents an arresting vision of a world in which time is porous and people are duplicated. Like Mandel's prior novels, it's ingenious, eerie and complex — and it hits close to home.

item.title: How to fight with the people we care about, illustrated
item.description: Arguing with a partner or a loved one can be anxiety-inducing. Conflict resolution facilitator Priya Parker explains how to start and end a fight — while easing dread for everyone.

item.title: Colin Kaepernick reflects on Jay-Z 'disappointing' him, losing the NFL and finding his power
item.description: A decade after taking a knee, Colin Kaepernick has no regrets and is reflecting on his life in his new memoir, The Perilous Fight. He talks to NPR's Michel Martin about losing football, his disappointment with Jay-Z and what the protest taught him about power.
item.content:encoded:
A decade after taking a knee, Colin Kaepernick has no regrets and is reflecting on his life in his new memoir, The Perilous Fight. He talks to NPR's Michel Martin about losing football, his disappointment with Jay-Z and what the protest taught him about power.

(Image credit: Noam Galai)

item.title: The legacy that Smithsonian head Lonnie Bunch leaves
item.description: Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch announced Tuesday that he's retiring at the end of the year. Bunch says his timing has nothing to do with attacks on the Smithsonian from the Trump administration.

item.title: Smithsonian Secretary on his retirement and the future of the organization
item.description: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Lonnie G. Bunch, III, the Smithsonian Secretary, who announced he is retiring after 38 years of service with the institution. He will step down at the end of the year.

item.title: Smithsonian chief Lonnie G. Bunch III resigns
item.description: Bunch has spent the last few months defending the Smithsonian against attacks from President Trump. In a statement, Bunch says he leaves with "mixed emotions."
